prs.title: Make the ZEPHYRUS escape dispatcher the default escape scheme
prs.author: maraattia
prs.body: ## Description Makes the ZEPHYRUS escape regime dispatcher the default escape scheme of PROTEUS (`escape.zephyrus.scheme = "dispatcher"`), with energy-limited escape kept as `"el"`. Closes #1038. - The dispatcher reads the atmosphere column of the last converged climate solve, which AGNI and JANUS now keep on `Atmos_t` (`atmos_clim/escape_profile.py`), so escape at step n reads the column of step n - 1. With the dummy atmosphere, under AGNI's transparent mode, and before the first converged solve, it reads an isothermal column at `T_eqm`, and an envelope too weakly bound for that column gets a short closed-form one out to twice the surface radius, which the dispatcher reads as boil-off. `esc_profile_source` records which column each step read. - It returns a rate per element. The `pxuv` reservoir, until now reserved, debits each element its rate share, capped at what the atmosphere holds of it, and the 25% step cap stays. - Over a frozen mantle no outgassing step re-forms the gases, so each gas loses its share of the escaping elements (`outgas/fractionated_debit.py`). Leftover O, H, N, and S form O2, H2, N2, and S2, carbon pairs into CO and then CH4, and carbon without a partner condenses as graphite into `C_kg_condensed` (tracked in `esc_graphite_kg`). Rock vapour keeps its mass, so on that path the step cap and the escaping shares count only the elements the gases can lose. - New helpfile columns: `esc_regime`, `esc_rate_branch`, `esc_kn_sonic`, `esc_lambda`, `esc_T_exo`, `

prs.title: Free compiled JAX programs after each structure re-solve
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description A coupled run with the Aragog interior and Zalmoxis structure re-solves stops on Linux after about 6 re-solves. Each re-solve updates the Aragog solver in place, Aragog compiles its JAX programs again, and the programs of the previous structure stay mapped in the process. The process then reaches the memory-map limit of Linux (`vm.max_map_count`, 65530 by default), and XLA fails with `LLVM compilation error: Cannot allocate memory`. This PR calls `jax.clear_caches()` after each accepted structure re-solve, only with the Aragog interior and only when JAX is already imported. A failed clear is logged as a warning and does not reject the accepted structure. The re-solve itself does not change. This is a mitigation, and the helper on this branch has not run on Habrok itself (the probe below runs the same call at the same point). Memory still grows by about 3.6 MiB per re-solve, and a structure solve after a giant impact (`accretion/wrapper.py`) does not clear the caches. The proper fix is to build the jitted functions once at module level in Aragog and pass the structure as data, which removes this helper again. ## Validation of changes Habrok probe on the paper-1 PROTEUS base `da4a85e2` plus a probe commit (`9aa8116e`) that calls `jax.clear_caches()` at the same point after an accepted re-solve and logs the map count and RSS, switched by an environment variable. 1 Earth mass coupled run (Aragog, Zalmoxis re-solves every 100 yr, AGNI, CALLIOPE, ZEPHYRUS, MORS), the

prs.title: Add the adiabat melt model and backend options to the boundary interior
prs.author: rdc49
prs.body: ## Description Updates to the boundary interior energetics module, including the option to calculate the mantle melt fraction by comparing an adiabatic mantle temperature profile to pressure-dependent melting curves. **The default cooling of the boundary backend changes.** `heat_capacity` no longer adds the latent term of the solidification front to a wholly molten mantle: above the liquidus the front sits at the core-mantle boundary and nothing freezes, so the latent heat it drew there was spurious (`test_dT_pdt_excludes_latent_heat_from_a_wholly_molten_mantle`). Every other default trajectory is unchanged: `melt_model` defaults to `"linear"`, and the new keys below default to the behaviour on `main`. prs.title: Default the mixing length to constant and add the Aragog mesh keys
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description The mixing length sets how far a convecting parcel of mantle rock moves before it mixes; Aragog and SPIDER turn it into an eddy diffusivity, which carries the convective heat flux. At the core-mantle boundary (CMB) the solver gives the CMB node the eddy diffusivity of the node above it. With the length `nearest` (the distance to the nearer boundary), that diffusivity falls to 0 when the node above turns stable, and in the runs below the heat flux out of the core then stays near 0 for 27 to 30 kyr on 2 of 3 meshes ( With `constant` (0.25 of the mantle depth at every node) none of the 4 meshes loses the flux for longer than 1 output row. What changes: 1. `interior_energetics.mixing_length` defaults to `constant` for Aragog and SPIDER. A SPIDER run without the key now gets `-mixing_length 2` instead of 1. Five input files that set `nearest` as a copy of the old default (`all_options`, `reducing`, `planets/mercury`, `tutorials/tutorial_vapourise`, `inference/example`) now set `constant`. 2. Three new Aragog keys: `interior_energetics.aragog.cmb_cell_thickness` (default 3000 m) and `surface_cell_thickness` (default `"uniform"`), passed to the mesh of and `rheology.mlt_bottom_slope` (default 1.0, the slope of the viscous-branch mixing length above the CMB). Each refuses a bool, a non-finite value and a value out of range. So the default mesh changes from the uniform mesh to one with a 3000 m cell at the CMB. 3. A resume checks the recorded mixing length like the sepa

prs.author: nichollsh
prs.body: ## Description Offline chemistry for Interra-Project/collaboration#80 needs to run at chosen states of the evolution, and with a climate that belongs to the computed composition. prs.title: Hold melt volatiles under a closed crust with a lid seal
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description This adds an optional lid seal to the outgassing step, `[outgas.lid_seal]`, off by default. Without it, the chemistry solve keeps the melt in equilibrium with the atmosphere at every step, even under a thick crust. With `enabled = true`, the dissolved inventory moves to new `{x}_kg_sealed` columns once the crust is at least `delta_close` thick (default 10 km) and the top mesh cell holds less than `phi_close` of melt (default 0.3). While the seal holds, the chemistry is frozen and the held volatiles reach the atmosphere only by a leak toward a floor, the mass that the melt dissolves at the current atmosphere: $$\frac{dM_i}{dt} = -\left(\frac{1}{\tau} + k_i\right) \max\left(M_i - M_{\mathrm{eq},i},\ 0\right), \qquad k_i = \frac{\chi_d \dot M_c}{R_i}$$ - The first term relaxes the held mass with `tau_leak`. The default is infinite, so nothing leaks. - The second term is volcanism at the rate `crust_rate` (default 0). It has the form of Eq. 14 and 17 of Schaefer & Sasselov (2015), with `chi_d` = 0.02 from their Table 3, and degasses only the excess over solubility. - The floor uses the CALLIOPE solubility laws and is taken at the end state of each step, so a long step cannot leak past it. With front trapping the floor also counts the solid formed since closure, at the effective partition (1 - F_tl) D + F_tl that trapping buries. - The seal opens again when the top cell holds `phi_open` of melt (default phi_close + 0.05), when the crust is thinner than `delta_open`

prs.title: Give each PROTEUS install its own Julia depot
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description Follows and Continues to create fully isolated PROTEUS environments per install so two installs do not interfere with each other. Two PROTEUS installs on one machine shared their Julia packages and compile files in `~/.julia`, so a package change in one reached the other. With this PR, `install.sh` keeps them in `$CONDA_PREFIX/julia_depot` and sets `JULIA_DEPOT_PATH` to that folder with a trailing colon, which keeps the compile files that come with Julia and does not add `~/.julia`. The Julia binary stays with juliaup, because conda-forge has no Julia for Apple Silicon. No result of a run should change, and no physics file changes. - A `JULIA_DEPOT_PATH` that is already set stays, with 2 exceptions: a `julia_depot` of another PROTEUS install is replaced, and so is one whose folder is gone from an `envs` folder. A value that is relative, names another user's home folder or holds a literal `$` stops the installer before it creates anything, and the message names the way out. - A value of your own now gives a warning. `bash install.sh -i` in a terminal asks `Use a Julia depot of its own for this install?` (default no), and `--ignore-julia-depot-path` keeps the value with one info line and no warning, except the depot of another install or of a gone environment. The installer never edits a shell start file and asks nothing without `-i` or a terminal, so CI and clusters see no question. - The installer and the doctor read the Julia manifest of a project by the 4 nam

prs.title: Couple the Aragog sub-grid lid to the atmosphere surface
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description A crust that forms at the surface of a magma ocean starts metres thick or less, while the top cell of the Aragog mesh is kilometres thick. Aragog models such a crust as a sub-grid lid (FormingWorlds/aragog#100, with the surface of an atmosphere from FormingWorlds/aragog#108; released in fwl-aragog 26.11.8). This PR couples that lid to the surface balance of PROTEUS. It is off by default. With `interior_energetics.aragog.lid_mush_base = true`: - PROTEUS runs the Aragog lid with its base at the solidus. The lid needs the Aragog solid rheology, which this PR exposes as `interior_energetics.aragog.rheology.enabled` (default false). - The atmosphere call (AGNI or the dummy) sees the lid and the open surface as two conductors in parallel at one surface temperature. `lid_boundary` in `atmos_clim/common.py` writes this sum as one skin, so neither atmosphere module changes its surface balance. - Aragog holds the lid surface at the `T_surf` of the last atmosphere call. Where the lid would then conduct more than the atmosphere took from the lid part, the lid surface warms and loses that flux plus the slope of `F_atm` times the warming. The slope comes from the last 2 rows. With the dummy, the step runs once more with the secant slope across the step when it differs; AGNI keeps the row slope. - Under a lid, `F_int` is the mean surface flux of the step from the Aragog energy integral, so the energy the lid stores or releases is booked. - Each interior snapshot stores the li

prs.title: Default to a 3000 m CMB cell and the uniform top cell
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description The mesh decides the thickness of the bottom cell, and the CMB heat flux of the core module is taken across half of that cell. On the uniform 80-node mesh that cell is 36.6 km thick for an Earth mantle. In a solid-mantle case with the core module, that mesh gives a CMB heat flux about a third below that of a uniform 640-node mesh. With a 3000 m bottom cell, the 80-node mesh is 0.45 % and 0.35 % below it at 50 and 100 Myr. What changes: 1. `mesh.cmb_cell_thickness` defaults to 3000 m (was 0, the uniform mesh). A value at or above the bottom cell of the uniform mesh of the same coordinate mode, or less than 1e-5 below it, gives no CMB refinement and one INFO line, so a coarse mesh falls back to its uniform bottom cell instead of being refused. 0 still means no CMB refinement. 2. `mesh.surface_cell_thickness` takes `"uniform"` (the new default: the top cell of the uniform mesh), 0, or a value in [2 m, uniform cell). A larger value is still refused. 3. The two-sided stretching starts at the uniform-cell limit without a bracket failure and refuses a pair of end cells that no stretching can reach. A refused refined mesh names the uniform mesh as the way out. 4. Tests that compare with uniform-mesh references now set the uniform mesh explicitly. 5. Docs: the mesh refinement explanation, how-to and Validation pages describe the default and its fallback, with a new case that compares the default with finer uniform meshes. prs.title: Stop the core energy budget from recompiling every step
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description A coupled run with the core module (`core_bc = "core_module"`, solid rheology on) recompiled parts of the core energy budget at every step: the inner-core boundary bisection closed over `t_cmb`, and the batched regime check and shell-base check ran at the length of each new state. Each compile adds memory maps to the process, and on a Habrok node the run died with `LLVM compilation error: Cannot allocate memory` (job 34327315, node limit `vm.max_map_count` 65530). - `_r_icb_bisect`: the loop body is built once per budget (`cached_property`) and `t_cmb` rides in the loop carry, so the loop compiles once. - The regime check pads its batch to a power of two (at least 8) by repeating the states in order (`np.resize`); the shell-base check and the layer base of the stratified core heat go through `_padded_call`, which pads to a power of two by repeating the last state. Each result is cut back to the input length, so each path compiles once per length bucket. - `tests/test_core_budget_compile_once.py` counts the compiles of each path and checks the padded results against the unpadded calls. ## Validation of changes - Habrok, the same coupled config at 275684d0 of this branch (the bisection fix and the regime-check padding; the later commits add the shell-base and layer-base padding): the job completes (exit 0) at step 162. prs.title: Update the temperature during a run through a climate hook
prs.author: nichollsh
prs.body: ## Description The AGNI coupling inside the VULCAN integration did not work: - It failed on AGNI 1.15, which no longer has the `plot_jacobian` keyword or the `solver.ls_increase` global. - After AGNI changed the temperature, nothing that depends on it was recomputed: rate constants, number densities, molecular diffusion, saturation and Kzz were all set once at the start. - `solve_rce = False` replaced the temperature with a dry adiabat. - AGNI was found only in `VULCAN/AGNI`, and the logger of a caller that had loaded AGNI already was replaced. VULCAN calls it before integrating, every `agni_call_frq` steps and at each steady state. - `Integration.update_climate` interpolates the profiles in log pressure onto the VULCAN grid. It keeps the mixing ratios, sets n = p / (k_B T), and recomputes rates, molecular diffusion, saturation, scale heights, settling and photolysis as at the start of a run. The element totals of the conservation check are rescaled, keeping the loss accumulated so far. - An update that changes T by more than `agni_T_rtol` restarts the step size from `dttry` and the steady-state window. prs.title: Accept only the full adiabat in adiabatic modes and seed the re-solve
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Description In the adiabatic temperature modes the Newton outer solver returned its root on the linear first guess of the temperature, with only a warning (`main`, Newton branch). A PROTEUS run with the Newton outer solver (its default) starts from such a solve whenever Zalmoxis computes the adiabat itself, so the initial mantle temperature was the linear guess, not the adiabat. With this change a solve in an adiabatic mode is accepted only on the full adiabat. - Full-adiabat rule: in `adiabatic` and `adiabatic_from_cmb` a result counts as converged only when its temperature is the full adiabat on a table built on a full-adiabat pass. After a Newton root, `main` continues with the adiabat blend ramp from that profile at the Newton mass tolerance. A ramp after a Newton root always retries when it does not converge; it never takes the 7 % retry skip. - Secant tail: at the end of the blend ramp the radius update takes secant steps instead of the cube-root rule, which cuts the full-adiabat passes of the first solve. - Seeded re-solve: `main` takes `adiabat_seed` (radii, pressure and enclosed mass of an earlier solve of the same planet) and starts from it at blend 1. A seeded solve that raises or does not converge runs again without the seed. A bad radius guess and a loose reference raise explicit errors. - Stored grid start-up reference: `tools/validation/grid_start_up_reference.py` solves the PROTEUS grid case (core mass fraction 0.95, 0.7 Earth masses) at a mass tolerance of

prs.title: Md/fluid tides
prs.author: MarijnJ0
prs.body: ## Description This PR adds the new `fluid1d_relax` tides model. It is a drag-poro-viscoelastic model which solves for shear, bulk, Darcy, and drag dissipation across solid, mush, and fluid layers. The model nolonger relies on segmentation and combination of Love numbers using loading Love numbers, and rather solves the entire column in one go. This means that the layering can be fairy arbitrary, unlike the previous versions of solid+fluid tides in Obliqua. Additionally many small fixes were added, energy closure/passivity is now achieved across a wide range of the tested parameter space (using Float64). Further improvements can be gained by setting the numerical precision to Bigfloat. The new solver has a slightly different code structure, this was mainly due to the fact that it brings small perfomance improvements. Since Obliqua will soon be applied to larger planets and include the Rotating Earth theory corrections for spin, I am slowly moving to a new structure. In a follow up PR I will also port the older solvers to the new structure. Related issue, but still misses spin effects. See the Overleaf doc for plots. Figure 1 there shows how `fluid1d_relax` perfectly matches both the solid and fluid tide analytical limits. Tests have been updated and are passing. prs.title: Give venting and the compaction divergence the spherical face weights
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview With `geometry.spherical_flow = true` the continuity rows (#141) and the momentum rows (#142) hold the balances of the spherical slice: each face flux of a P cell enters with the multiplier $m_F = w_F / w_P$ of its 3-D area. Two other terms read the same face fluxes in the 2-D form: the venting surface flux, which enters the fluid continuity row of the rock cell, and the solid divergence that sets the compaction pressure of the melt segregation. Venting was therefore refused with the option. This PR gives both terms the multipliers of the continuity rows and allows venting with the option. The fluid heat advection keeps the 2-D form: its upwind term is the advective form $-(\rho c_p)_f \mathbf{q}_D \cdot \nabla T$, which has no divergence, and $m_F$ on its inflow faces gives an error of $(m_W - 1)$ times the term, which does not fall with the grid spacing near the centre. For the user: with the option off nothing changes. With the option on, venting runs, and the vented rate and the compaction pressure use the spherical face areas. ## Changes - `src/numerics/thermal.jl` (+34, -1): `apply_venting_surface_boundary!` takes the keyword `spherical_flow` and multiplies the conductance of each open face by $m_F$ of that face of the rock cell (`_venting_face_weight`), so the matrix entry, the right-hand side, the rate `S_vent_out` and the drain limit use the weighted rate. A non-finite centre with the option throws. - `src/numerics/segregation.jl` (+74, -24): the solid di

prs.title: Spherical momentum with the out-of-plane stress (geometry.spherical_flow)
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview With `geometry.spherical_flow = true` (PR #141) the continuity rows hold the spherical mass balance, but the momentum rows stay 2-D plane strain. For a radial flow $v_r \propto 1/r^2$, which is divergence free in a sphere, the 2-D momentum balance then gives a total pressure that varies as $1/r^3$, where a sphere has a uniform $P_t$. This pressure enters the effective pressure $P_t - P_f$ and the hydrofracture criterion. This PR gives the momentum rows the slice form of the same option: $$\frac{1}{w} \partial_j (w \tau_{ij}) - \tau_{33} \frac{\partial_i w}{w} - \partial_i P_t + \rho g_i = 0, \quad w = 2r,$$ the momentum equation of the spherical annulus with $d = 2$ (Hernlund and Tackley 2008). The pressure part of the weighted stress divergence cancels against the pressure part of $\sigma_{33}$, so $P_t$ stays unweighted. For a radial flow the equation is $\partial_r \sigma_{rr} + (2\sigma_{rr} - \sigma_{\phi\phi} - \sigma_{33})/r$, the radial balance of a sphere. The stress is the 3-D deviatoric one, $\tau_{ij} = 2\eta(\dot\varepsilon_{ij} - \delta_{ij} \nabla_3 \cdot \mathbf{u}/3)$, with $\dot\varepsilon_{33} = \mathbf{u} \cdot \nabla w / w$. The code stores one new component: `SXX` keeps its meaning $(\tau_{xx} - \tau_{yy})/2$, the quantity the 2-D code already evolves, and `S33` $= \tau_{33}$ is added with its own visco-elastic history on the grid and the markers. Then $\tau_{xx} = S_{xx} - S_{33}/2$ and $\tau_{yy} = -S_{xx} - S_{33}/2$. An in-plane rotation

prs.title: Spherical face weights in the continuity rows (geometry.spherical_flow)
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview With the defaults `geometry.spherical_metric = true` and `geometry.gravity_mode = :enclosed_mass`, Erebus uses the spherical term of heat conduction and enclosed-mass gravity, but the mass balance of the flow stays the one of a 2-D disk. The continuity rows of the Stokes-Darcy system take the plain 2-D divergence of the solid velocity and of the Darcy flux. A uniform radial outflow then loses mass at the rate of a cylinder, not of a sphere: for a Darcy flux driven by a pressure of the form $a r^2$ the 2-D divergence is $4 a k / \eta_f$, the 3-D value is $6 a k / \eta_f$. This PR adds the option `geometry.spherical_flow` (off by default). With it on, each face term of the solid and fluid continuity rows is multiplied by the face weight $w_F / w_P$ with $w = 2 r$, from `flow_metric_face_weights`. The rows then hold the flux form $\nabla \cdot (w \mathbf{u}) / w_P$, which is the continuity equation of an annulus with $d = 2$ (Hernlund and Tackley 2008, Eq. 1). Neighbouring cells evaluate $w_F$ at the same face, so the sum of $w_P$ times the weighted divergence over the weighted cells telescopes to the flux through their outer faces. For the user: with the option off, the assembled matrix and right-hand side are bitwise unchanged. With the option on, the run needs `spherical_metric = true`, the direct solver, no MPI and no surface venting; the config validation refuses the other cases. Momentum stays 2-D, and some other readers of the divergence stay on the disk (see

prs.title: Use the solve resistances for Darcy friction heating
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview With hydrofracture on, the Darcy friction term of the shear heating did not belong to the Darcy fluxes it was computed with. The Stokes-Darcy solve computes `qxD` and `qyD` with face resistances from the pressures before the solve of the last plastic pass, including the `theta_frac` relaxation, `ramp_width` and `rx_floor_prefactor`. `compute_shear_heating!` then recomputed the hydrofracture resistance of each face from the pressures after the solve, without those options. Where a fracture face opens or closes between the two pressure states, the heating `r q^2` uses a resistance that the fluxes do not satisfy. This PR passes the resistances of the solve to the heating. The heating of each face is then the work of the discrete Darcy law on that face. For the user: no new option. Runs with `poroelasticity.hydrofracture = true` change by a small amount once fracture faces open; runs without hydrofracture do not change. ## Changes - `src/physics/dissipation.jl`: `compute_shear_heating!` drops its hydrofracture recompute and the keywords for it. The positional `RX`, `RY` are the resistances the fluxes were solved with. The function now checks that every P-node array, the resistances and the fluxes have the size of `HS`, and `ETA`, `SXY` one row and column less (`ArgumentError`), since the loop runs with `inbounds`. - Breaking change: `compute_shear_heating!` is exported and no longer takes the keywords `hydrofracture`, `TEN`, `KX`, `KY`, `PHIX`, `PHIY`, `kphim0`, `phim

prs.title: Accelerate the plastic loop with Anderson mixing
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview Under fluid overpressure the plastic Picard loop in `solve_stokes_darcy!` often does not settle: a few nodes in tensile yield jump between two states, and the loop either runs into the cycle stop of #138 or into `max_plastic_iterations`. Each such attempt fails and the step retries with half the time step. In `hydrothermal_benchmark` this happens in 104 of 1319 loop calls over 400 steps, and on the 129 x 129 grid of `hydrothermal_reaction_on_128` the run aborts at step 110 with a `PlasticConvergenceError` after five time step cuts in a row. This PR accelerates the loop with Anderson mixing (the type II update of Walker & Ni 2011). After each pass the next state is a least-squares combination of the last few passes instead of the last pass alone. The solve and the yield update of a pass do not change, so a converged state satisfies the same yield test as on main. Because an accelerated loop no longer repeats its states, a stagnation stop ends a loop whose yield residual has not reached a new minimum for `solver.plastic_stall_passes` passes. For the user: the benchmark reaches 0.02904 Myr in 400 steps instead of 0.02535 Myr, with 23 failed loop calls instead of 104, and the 129 x 129 reaction run gets past the step where main aborts. Two new options, `solver.anderson_depth` (default `5`, `0` gives the plain loop) and `solver.plastic_stall_passes` (default `1000`). The acceleration is on by default, so results of runs with plastic yielding change within the loop tole

prs.title: Stop the plastic loop when its state cycles
prs.author: timlichtenberg
prs.body: ## Overview When a few nodes sit in tensile yield under fluid overpressure, the plastic Picard loop in `solve_stokes_darcy!` can fall into a limit cycle: the viscosity, the solution and the residual repeat with a period of a few passes and never reach `yerrmax`. On main the loop then runs all `max_plastic_iterations` (10000) passes before the step fails and retries with half the time step. In `hydrothermal_benchmark` this happens in 104 attempts over 400 steps, and those passes dominate the run time. This PR ends the loop as not converged as soon as its carried state is periodic. The step then fails and retries with half the time step, exactly as it does on main after 10000 passes, so the accepted step sequence does not change. For the benchmark the accepted time steps and the final state are bitwise equal to main, and the run takes 509 s instead of about 2 h 10 min. The check is controlled by a new option `solver.plastic_cycle_window` (default `10`, `0` turns it off). The stop must never end a loop that would converge on main, so the test is strict: every tracked value of every pass of the run has to match, to a relative tolerance of 1e-9, both the pass one period earlier and the earliest pass of the same phase in the run. ## Changes - Cycle tracker (`src/numerics/plasticity.jl`, +345): `PlasticCycleTracker`, `reset_plastic_cycle!` and `plastic_cycle_record!`. releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: This release changes the default mesh, so runs that leave out the CMB and surface cell settings give other results than with 26.11.08. Changes to results and defaults: - `mesh.cmb_cell_thickness` defaults to 3000 m and `mesh.surface_cell_thickness` to the top cell of the uniform mesh (#116). On a mesh too coarse for a 3000 m cell, the bottom cell of the uniform mesh is used, with one INFO line. Set both to 0 for the uniform mesh. - With `phase_boundary_cap = 'rate'`, a solid mantle with a heating cell near its solidus no longer integrates at 100 yr steps; the segment ends at the solidus instead (#109). Fixes: - A coupled run with the core module and the solid rheology no longer recompiles the core energy budget at every step, which ran out of memory maps on long Linux runs (#112). - The per-call DEBUG lines that logged whole arrays are gone, so the file log of a long run stays small (#111). - Under `core_bc = 'core_module'`, an INFO line says that `boundary_conditions.core_heat_capacity` and `mesh.core_density` are not used (#110). Known limit: the CMB heat flux of the core module still depends on the thickness of the bottom cell in the solid regime. A boundary-layer law that does not depend on the mesh is in work.

releases.author: maraattia
releases.body: An escape regime dispatcher. `zephyrus.dispatch` takes one planetary state and an atmosphere profile and returns the escape regime (boil-off, a hydrodynamic wind limited by energy, recombination, or photons, hydrostatic Jeans escape, or Roche-lobe overflow), a bulk mass-loss rate, a rate for each species through a diffusion closure that separates light from heavy elements, flags for every approximation the call made, and diagnostics of how close the state sat to each regime boundary. `EL_escape` stays available at its old import path. The documentation describes each regime, its criteria, and its validation, and has a standalone tutorial. The hydrostatic branch starts its upper structure from the log-pressure mean temperature of the top 3 pressure decades of the profile (`T_anchor_decades`), and the "ZEPHYRUS in PROTEUS" page describes the coupling that PROTEUS uses. `Fxuv_earth_10Myr` is now 0.628 W m⁻², the young-Sun value of the cited model; no code reads it. ## What's Changed * Use the fwl-io cache commands for the nightly data cache by timlichtenberg in * Sync the shared AGENTS.md block with the validation rules by timlichtenberg in * Add the student layout rule for Validation pages to AGENTS.md by timlichtenberg in * Add an escape regime dispatcher with per-species fractionation by maraattia in * Cite papers in the docs with one footnote form by timlichtenberg in * Set Fxuv_earth_10Myr to the young-Sun XUV flux of the cited model by timlichtenberg in * Let the docs work

releases.author: timlichtenberg
releases.body: Zalmoxis now accepts a structure solve in an adiabatic mode only when its temperature is the full adiabat, and seeds the re-solve from the accepted structure (#133). The outer loop stops on a stalled mass oscillation (#114), the central-pressure root is refined when it misses the surface pressure (#122), and every accepted structure result is checked against its physical invariants (#113). The padded surface node gets its EOS density and Gauss gravity (#115), and the docs state when the pressure solve accepts a padded profile (#119). Cores can carry H, C, N, O, Si and S (#121), with the alloy density calibrated on the Hirose 2021 outer cores (#127). A standalone run writes every file into one output folder (#129), and the DEBUG profile dump goes only into a folder the caller names (#128). The loggers are named under fwl, so PROTEUS captures the Zalmoxis logs (#120). A new check tests the thermodynamic identities of an EOS table (#112). PALEOS is pinned at the rewritten tested commit (#117), a PALEOS main ahead of that commit gives a warning instead of a failure (#118), and a missing fwl-io is reported as missing instead of as a stale table (#111). Validation is now a docs tab, rewritten for students with plots (#116, #124, #125). CI pins Python 3.12 (#123), the nightly wolfbower tests are spread over all workers (#126), and the slow tests are bounded by per-test limits instead of the solver clock (#130).

entries.title: New Aragog mixing length and mesh defaults
entries.text: Aragog and SPIDER now use a constant mixing length by default, and the default Aragog mesh has a thin cell at the core-mantle boundary. Runs that leave these settings out give a different core heat flux than before. In the cases tested, the old setting could stall the heat flux out of the core for tens of kyr.

entries.title: Radionuclide inputs redefined
entries.text: The radionuclide concentrations are now total element concentrations, and the isotope mass ratios are separate config fields. The defaults for both changed, so an existing config gives different radiogenic heating unless it is reviewed.

entries.title: Zalmoxis start-up structure on the full adiabat
entries.text: In the adiabatic modes, Zalmoxis now accepts a structure only when its temperature is the full adiabat, not the linear first guess. PROTEUS requires this Zalmoxis release and seeds each start-up re-solve from the last structure, so initial mantle temperatures can differ from earlier runs.

entries.title: Hydrostatic escape anchored on a mean temperature
entries.text: The hydrostatic branch of the ZEPHYRUS dispatcher now starts from a log-pressure mean temperature of the top of the profile, not the single topmost level. Rates change only where the top of the profile is not isothermal.

entries.title: ZEPHYRUS escape regime dispatcher
entries.text: ZEPHYRUS can now choose the escape regime for a planetary state and atmosphere profile. It returns a bulk mass-loss rate and a rate for each species, with flags for the approximations used.

entries.title: Offline chemistry at chosen evolution states
entries.text: Offline chemistry can now run at states picked by helpfile values such as melt fraction or surface temperature, with one run for each crossing. VULCAN can be coupled to the AGNI climate, so the temperature follows the computed composition.

entries.title: Lid seal for melt volatiles
entries.text: An optional seal holds dissolved volatiles in the melt once a closed crust has formed, and releases them by a leak or by volcanism. It is off by default, so existing runs do not change.

entries.title: Aragog sub-grid crust lid coupled to the atmosphere
entries.text: Aragog can model a thin surface crust as a sub-grid lid, coupled to the surface balance of the atmosphere module. It is off by default and needs the Aragog solid rheology.

entries.title: Spherical flow and a faster plastic loop in Erebus
entries.text: Erebus can now use spherical mass and momentum balances for the flow, including venting. The plastic loop is faster and ends sooner when it cycles. Darcy friction heating now uses the same resistances as the flow solve.

entries.title: Separate Julia depot for each PROTEUS install
entries.text: Each PROTEUS install now keeps its Julia packages in its own folder, so two installs on one machine no longer change each other. The installer warns when you have set your own depot path.

entries.title: VULCAN must be installed from its clone
entries.text: VULCAN needs data files that a package install does not provide, so CI now installs it from its clone. A VULCAN install without the data fails early with a message that names the install script. On macOS, a star file path that is too long for the SOCRATES tools is now refused with a clear error.

entries.title: Memory fixes for long coupled runs on Linux
entries.text: Coupled runs with Aragog and repeated structure solves ran out of memory maps on Linux because compiled programs piled up. PROTEUS now frees the compiled programs after each accepted structure solve, and Aragog no longer recompiles the core energy budget at every step. This is a mitigation, and memory still grows slowly.

entries.title: Two core masses in the structure output
entries.text: A Zalmoxis solve has the core mass it was given and the mass inside the core radius, which also holds some mantle silicate. PROTEUS keeps the second as the core mass and adds a new column for the first. A rejected structure update restores both.

entries.title: Climate hook between VULCAN and a climate model
entries.text: VULCAN now takes a climate hook that returns updated temperature profiles during a run. VULCAN recomputes rates, diffusion and photolysis after each update. This replaces the direct AGNI coupling that failed on current AGNI.

entries.title: ZEPHYRUS dispatcher as the default escape scheme
entries.text: This open pull request makes the dispatcher the default escape scheme, with energy-limited escape kept as an option. The escape step reads the atmosphere column of the last converged climate solve and debits each element by its share.

entries.title: Adiabat melt model for the boundary interior
entries.text: This open pull request adds a melt model from a mantle adiabat and new options for the boundary interior module. It also changes the default cooling of a wholly molten boundary mantle, which then cools faster than before.

entries.title: Fluid tides model in Obliqua
entries.text: This open pull request adds a tides model that solves shear, bulk, Darcy and drag dissipation across solid, mush and fluid layers in one solve. It allows arbitrary layering.
